title: Congenital Nasolacrimal Duct Obstruction (CNLDO): Clinical Mastery
summary: A comprehensive clinical guide to the management and diagnostic assessment of congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction in infants. This resource covers everything from the bedside Dye Disappearance Test to surgical intervention protocols.

sections.title: DDT Methodology & Interpretation
sections.content: Fluorescein 1% is instilled into each lower conjunctival fornix and cobalt blue light from the slitlamp illuminates the eyes. Tear meniscus is evaluated at 5 minutes. Normally, fluorescein disappears from the tear meniscus by 5 minutes, but remains present in children with obstruction.

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Phase 1: Conservative (First year of life; high spontaneous resolution). Includes Crigler massage.
Phase 2: Antibiotics (Only if conjunctivitis present; avoid in watery white eyes).
Phase 3: Dacryocystitis requires systemic antibiotics and urgent probing with attention to marsupialization of the membranous cyst.
Phase 4: Syringing and Probing (At >1 year of age; 90% success rate).
Phase 5: NLD Intubation with silicone stents (If probing fails).
Phase 6: DCR (Indicated for persistent epiphora after probing/intubation).

sections.title: Surgical Technique: Probing
content: Technique: Pass through upper/lower punctum after dilation, advance along canaliculus with gentle lateral lid traction.
Anatomical milestone: Reach nasal bone, rotate 90 degrees, introduce into NLD, advance into nose.
Tactile feedback: 'Gritty' feeling in stenotic ducts; 'pop' indicates distal membrane breach.
Adjunct: Inferior turbinate may be fractured medially if under general anesthesia.
Confirmation: Metal-on-metal palpation, swallowing reflex (awake), suction of fluorescein-saline (anesthetized), or direct observation.
Efficacy: 70%–97% success rate (averaging ~90%); decreases after 24-36 months.

sections.title: Differential Diagnosis & Red Flags
content: Re-closure of surgically created DCR osteotomy
Congenital glaucoma (always rule out if corneal clouding/enlargement present)
